summary: Apache County, AZ lookout on Mount Baldy (Dzil Ligai) on the Fort Apache Reservation; staffed 1914-1918, abandoned 1958, rubble by 2004.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists it gone; a June 1, 2004 photo shows only a pile of rubble; the survey datasheet says the building was abandoned in 1958
facts.agency: White Mountain Apache Tribe (Fort Apache Indian Reservation); the reservation boundary runs part way up the eastern slope, where the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests begin

access.note: On the Fort Apache Indian Reservation. The tribe has designated the area around the sacred mountain as tribal wilderness, with activities that would damage it off-limits. No source describes a permit process for the lookout site.

events.note: The Supervisor could not station a lookout on the mountain because of snow near the summit; a lookout man was now on this point (St. Johns Herald and Apache News, May 28, 1914, reprinted by Forest Lookouts)

Forestry Department engaged Miss Crosby to take charge of the lookout station at the top for the season (St. Johns Observer item, reprinted by Forest Lookouts) The item names only Mt. Baldy or Old Baldy, so the link to this mountain rests on its St. Johns origin.
Survey datasheet says the building was abandoned in 1958

corrections.proposed: White Mountain Apache Tribe (Fort Apache Indian Reservation)
corrections.why: Peakbagging places the lookout site on the Fort Apache Indian Reservation and the Forest Service says the mountain is on the reservation's eastern edge. The Coronado heading on the Forest Lookouts page appears to come from its 1922-1928 items about a different Mount Baldy in the Santa Rita Mountains.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1918 St. Johns item gives nearly 12,000 feet. Peakbagging gives 11,403 ft for the lookout site and the Forest Service gives 11,421 ft for the mountain. The story uses the survey-based figures and notes the 1918 figure.

notes_for_editor: The Forest Lookouts Mount Baldy page mixes two mountains. The 1925 and 1928 items, and the 1922 Patagonia fire report, describe a Mount Baldy in the Santa Rita Mountains in Coronado NF; they are left out. The 1914 and 1918 items are tied to St. Johns and Eager, both in Apache County; the attribution to this lookout is by place, since the item names only Mt. Baldy or Old Baldy. The 1918 item's 12,000 ft figure conflicts with survey figures. An Arizona Highways article in search results says three-quarters of the mountain, including the summit, is on the reservation; it was not read in full, so it is not used. Access 'restricted' is inferred from the tribal wilderness rule; no permit process was found. Ownership is mixed (reservation with some national forest on the eastern slope), so the record's 'federal' ownership is not corrected here. No photos recorded; the Peakbagging photo page has no image URL in the cache.
